transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… the main thing is work. I’m an electrician, and lately I keep getting stuck going back over jobs again and again. Like I’ll finish an install, and instead of being able to trust that it’s done, I’m checking the breakers, then the labels, then the torque marks, then the photos I took, and sometimes I’ll still feel like I need to drive back to the site just to make sure I didn’t miss something.

And I know some checking is part of the job, obviously—it’s electrical work, you don’t want to be careless—but this is getting beyond that. A simple job that should be wrapped up pretty quickly ends up taking way longer because I keep rechecking the same things. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because people are starting to notice. I’m trying to look thorough, but it’s more like I can’t get myself to stop.
How do you feel if you’re unable to check the work as much as you’d like? Do you feel anxious or distressed?

Yeah, definitely. If I can’t check it the way I feel like I need to, I get really uneasy. It’s not just a normal “did I forget something?” feeling—it kind of sits in my chest and I keep replaying the job in my head.

Like, I’ll be thinking, okay, did I check the breaker? Did I label that correctly? Did I actually tighten that the way I remember, or am I just assuming I did? Then I’ll start looking at the photos I took, and even if the photos look fine, there’s still this nagging feeling like, “What if the thing I’m worried about isn’t visible in the picture?” And then sometimes I end up driving back to the site, because otherwise I can’t really let it go.

And I know that sounds excessive. I know electrical work has to be careful, and some checking is part of being responsible, but this is different. A simple install can take way longer than it should because I keep going back over the same stuff—breakers, labels, torque marks, pictures—over and over. If I’m stopped from doing that, or I try to force myself not to, I get pretty distressed until I can check again.
When you feel the need to go back and check your work, does it feel like you’re trying to prevent something bad from happening, like an accident or a mistake that could hurt someone?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of the feeling behind it, I think. It’s like I can’t just leave the job alone because I keep thinking, what if I missed something important? So I go back through the breakers, the labels, the torque marks, the photos I took—sometimes more than once, sometimes a bunch of times.

And it’s not like I don’t know how to do my job. I do. I’ve been doing this long enough to know what a proper check looks like. But lately it’s like the checking doesn’t “stick,” if that makes sense. I’ll check something, and then a few minutes later I’ll think, “Did I really check that?” or “What if I looked right at it and didn’t notice?” And then I feel like I have to go over it again.

Sometimes I’ll even leave the site and then the thought keeps bothering me so much that I’ll turn around or drive back later just to look again. A simple install ends up taking way longer than it should, and honestly people are starting to notice. I try to pass it off as being careful, but it feels more like I’m stuck in this loop and I can’t move on until I’ve checked enough.
When you’re going back over your work, are you having specific thoughts that feel intrusive or unwanted—like a fear that something bad will happen if you don’t check?

Yeah, that’s exactly it. It’s not just a general worry, it’s like a specific thought that barges in even after I know I checked something.

Like I’ll check a panel or a disconnect, and in the moment I can see that it’s done, but then this thought comes back: what if I missed one loose neutral? What if there’s one thing I didn’t catch and it heats up later, or starts a fire, or somebody gets hurt because I walked away too soon? And I’ll try to tell myself, “No, you checked it, you know what you’re doing,” but it doesn’t really settle.

It’s unwanted, definitely. I’m not sitting there trying to think of worst-case scenarios on purpose. It just kind of pushes its way in, and then I feel like I have to answer it somehow by checking again. Even if I leave the job, it’ll follow me all the way home. I’ll be driving and replaying the panel in my head, picturing the disconnect, wondering if I actually saw what I think I saw. It gets hard to trust my own memory of it.
When you go back to check your work, do you feel like you have to do it a certain way or in a specific order to feel reassured, or is it more about just making sure everything is physically correct?

It’s more about making sure everything is physically correct, I think… but I do end up doing it in a pretty repetitive way. Like I’ll go back over the breakers, then the labels, then the torque marks, then I’ll look at the photos I took, and sometimes I’ll do that whole thing more than once because I don’t feel settled after the first pass.

It’s not like I have some exact ritual where it has to be left-to-right or counted a certain number of times, at least I don’t think so. It’s more that I keep feeling like I didn’t really confirm it well enough. So I’ll check the same breaker again, or re-read the label again, or zoom in on a photo even though I already looked at it.

And if I’ve already left the site, that’s when it gets really frustrating, because sometimes I can’t let it go from just the pictures. I’ll think, “No, I need to actually see it again.” And then I’ll drive back, even if it’s inconvenient or makes me look ridiculous. That’s what’s been bringing me in, really—these jobs that should be simple end up taking way longer because I’m going back over them again and again, and people are starting to notice.
